Laravel 12 app: `laravel/framework` v12, `laravel/prompts` v0, `laravel/mcp` v0, `laravel/pint` v1, `laravel/sail` v1, `phpunit/phpunit` v11. Follow conventions; inspect siblings, use descriptive names, reuse components, preserve structure.

You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application.
Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works.
Stick to existing directory structure - don't create new base folders without approval.
Do not change the application's dependencies without approval.
You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.
Be concise.

Use Laravel Boost tools. Check Artisan parameters with `list-artisan-commands`; use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs, `tinker` for PHP debugging/direct Eloquent queries, `database-query` for read-only database access, and `browser-logs` for recent logs/errors/exceptions (ignore old logs).
Boost's `search-docs` tool returns version-specific Laravel ecosystem documentation. You must use this tool to search for Laravel-ecosystem documentation before falling back to other approaches.
Search the documentation before making code changes to ensure we are taking the correct approach.
Use multiple broad, simple, topic-based queries; no package names. Multiple queries are supported; search supports stemming, AND terms, quoted phrases, mixed terms, and multiple queries (any match).

Always use curly braces for control structures, even if it has one line.
Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`.
Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters.
Always use explicit return type declarations for methods and functions.
Use appropriate PHP type hints for method parameters.
Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless there is something _very_ complex going on.
Add useful array shape type definitions for arrays when appropriate.
Typically, keys in an Enum should be TitleCase.

Create files using `php artisan make:`; use `php artisan make:class` for generic PHP classes. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands to ensure they work without user input. You should also pass the correct `--options` to ensure correct behavior. Use `list-artisan-commands` to check available commands/options.
Use typed Eloquent relationships, ORM/model queries over `DB::` or raw queries, eager loading to prevent N+1s, and the query builder for very complex operations. Create useful factories and seeders for new models; ask if more are needed and check `php artisan make:model` options. For APIs, prefer versioned Eloquent API Resources unless existing routes use another convention. Use Form Requests (rules and custom messages), checking sibling rule style. Use `ShouldQueue` jobs for time-consuming work; Laravel auth/authorization; named route
